input.prompt: Use the reference image only as the style and craft reference: paint a NEW panel that is a sibling of it, with exactly the same lotus-and-vine border around all four edges (lotus-and-vine scroll between two thin dotted bands on ecru), the same deep madder red ground, the same dye palette, the same iron-black kalam line quality, the same dense dot, cross-hatch and scale fill patterns, and the same visible hand-woven cotton texture. An authentic Srikalahasti kalamkari hand-painted textile panel, photographed flat and straight-on so the cloth fills the entire frame edge to edge. Subject: a Telugu engagement ceremony (nischitartham). Across the top, a simple flat canopy (pandal) whose edge is hung with a festoon garland of mango leaves and marigold flowers. Below it stand exactly six people in one row, full figures from head to feet, drawn in the classical kalamkari manner: side or three-quarter profiles, large almond eyes, stylised hands, patterned drapery. At the centre, the young man (short black hair, neat short beard, round glasses, a plain cream kurta with white pyjama) stands on the left facing right, and the young woman (long black hair in a braid with white jasmine flowers, a madder red and indigo silk saree with a yellow border) stands on the right facing left; they face each other and each holds out one small ring toward the other, their hands near but not touching. On the far left, behind the young man, stand his two elders: an older man in a white dhoti with an angavastram over his shoulder and an older woman in an indigo saree. On the far right, behind the young woman, stand her two elders: an older woman in a green saree and an older man in a white dhoti with an angavastram. Each of the four elders holds one round plate of thambulam in both hands: betel leaves, bananas, a coconut, flowers and a folded silk saree. At the bottom, a band of small lotus flowers and leaves on the ground line. Style: freehand kalam (bamboo pen) outlines in iron-black with confident, slightly irregular line weight; flat natural vegetable-dye fills only: deep madder red (alizarin, brick red), indigo blue, myrobalan-turmeric yellow, green made from indigo over yellow, and areas of undyed ecru cotton; the skin of all figures is a flat ecru-ochre tone; dense hand-drawn fill patterns; visible hand-woven cotton weave and slight dye bleed at the edges of colour areas; the ground of the panel is dyed deep madder red. Every person has two arms, two hands with five fingers, and one face. Completely flat, no perspective, no shading, no gradients, no metallic gold, no 3D, no photorealism. No text, no letters, no writing, no script, no numbers, no inscriptions. No lamps, no diyas, no oil lamps, no candles, no fire, no flames anywhere.
